All _resolve_storage() fallbacks changed from LocalStorageBackend(root) to get_storage_backend(root) — respects STORAGE_BACKEND setting (R2 or local). Applies to content_data_service.py and brand_data_service.py.

_load_pipeline_state in content_data_service accepts optional storage= param. StorageBackend path tried first, legacy Path.read_text() kept as fallback when storage=None (migration window). db_content_data.py inline pipeline_state read also migrated to self._backend.read().

is_symlink() guard in content_data_service made conditional: only runs when backend is LocalStorageBackend (via getattr(sb, 'inner', sb) unwrap for CachedStorageBackend). R2 has no symlinks — StorageBackend._resolve() handles traversal protection.

task: Phase 3 — R2 Blob Storage Redis Cache Layer (4 changes)
decisions: Change 3.1: Replace Path.stat().st_mtime with JSON completed_at/started_at for audit sorting. ISO 8601 strings sort lexicographically — no datetime parsing needed. _sync_list_audits now loads ALL audit JSON (cached) then sorts, instead of mtime-sort-then-load-top-N.

Change 3.2+3.4: CachedStorageBackend calls get_sync_redis_or_none() per-operation (not constructor injection) — matches all service patterns and enables graceful degradation if Redis dies after startup. read_bytes() NOT cached due to decode_responses=True on Redis client requiring base64 encoding (33% overhead). exists() NOT cached (boolean, cheap, invalidation complexity). 512KB size guard prevents Redis bloat from large audit JSON files. None reads NOT cached (avoids stale negative entries). Empty list_dir results ARE cached (prevents repeated R2 ListObjectsV2). Shallow parent-only invalidation for list_dir (acceptable because list_dir returns immediate children only).

Change 3.3: _resolve_storage() pattern in brand_data_service matches content_data_service pattern. _detect_artifact and _detect_personas made positional-required for backend param — both are module-private, only called from get_research_artifacts.

Double-caching accepted: CachedStorageBackend (artifact:*) caches raw text at StorageBackend level; service-level caches (cache:gap:*, cache:content:*) cache parsed JSON with domain-specific TTLs. Intentional layering — CachedStorageBackend is general-purpose, service caches are domain-specific. Acceptable at current scale (<100 cache keys).
Cache key schema: artifact:{path} for reads, artifact_ls:{prefix} for list_dir. Avoids collision with existing cache:* prefix keys.

task: Phase 2 — Critical Redis Bug Fixes (6 fixes)
decisions: Fix 2.1: _init_attempted set AFTER success only; transient failures allow retry; connection_args passed to RedisSaver for timeout parity with core/redis.py
Fix 2.2: Each close_redis() close isolated in try/except; sync.close() via asyncio.to_thread to avoid blocking event loop; errors collected and logged as warning

Fix 2.3: Content cache key changed from cache:content:{full_path} to cache:content:{slug}:{colon-separated-relative} to match invalidation pattern; KEYS replaced with scan_iter+batched DELETE (500 batch size)
Fix 2.4: cleanup_stale when task_id=None changed from DELETE (clobber) to warning+skip; callers MUST pass task_id for scoped cleanup

Fix 2.5: Background _renewal_loop added to _SemaphoreContext — renews every 60s, started on acquire, cancelled on release; all 15 runners get automatic renewal; HITL heartbeat renewal kept as belt-and-suspenders (also renews slug lock)
Fix 2.6: _or_none helpers broadened from except RuntimeError to except Exception with logger.debug; prevents 20+ caller crash vectors
rationale: These are correctness bugs found by Codex audit that affect multi-worker deployments. Fixing before filesystem elimination phase to ensure Redis-first path is robust.

task: Redis Session 5 — Distributed Semaphore Design Decisions
approach: Atomic Lua script for acquire (ZREMRANGEBYSCORE+ZCARD+ZADD in single call). Sorted Set with timestamp scores for self-healing. pipeline_semaphore(task_id) method (Option B from spec — explicit task_id, not context magic). 2h holder TTL without heartbeat. 1s polling interval without pub/sub wake-up.
rationale: Codex review confirmed P0 race condition in spec's non-atomic acquire — Lua script prevents two workers both seeing capacity and both ZADD. Option B is explicit (task_id at each call site) vs Option C's contextvars magic. 2h TTL acceptable: pipelines run minutes-to-hours, max 3 concurrent, heartbeat adds complexity for marginal benefit. 1s polling irrelevant vs pipeline duration (minutes).
alternatives_rejected: Non-atomic acquire (separate ZREMRANGEBYSCORE/ZCARD/ZADD) — race condition under contention
Short lease + heartbeat renew — over-engineering for max 3 pipelines running minutes-to-hours
Pub/Sub wake-up on release — adds failure modes (missed messages) for no practical gain
Fencing tokens — semaphore gates starts not shared mutable state, unnecessary
Option C (contextvars for task_id) — too magical, implicit coupling
outcome: 11 new tests, 14 runner call sites updated, 1 Codex P0 finding resolved, zero regressions. 9th Redis key in schema.

task: Redis Integration Sessions 0-2 — Architecture Decisions
approach: Dual Redis clients (async for hot paths, sync for locks/reads). Config toggles per feature (REDIS_EVENT_BUS, REDIS_PIPELINE_STATE). Graceful fallback to file/in-memory when Redis unavailable. Atomic Lua scripts for EventBus (INCR+XADD) and lock release (compare-and-delete). Fail-closed distributed locks when Redis is configured.
rationale: Async client prevents event loop blocking in pipeline hot paths (6-8 state writes per run). Sync client acceptable for sub-ms lock ops and to_thread readers. Config toggles allow incremental rollout. Lua scripts guarantee atomicity without multi-step race conditions. Fail-closed prevents split-brain in multi-worker.
alternatives_rejected: Sync Redis everywhere — would block event loop on state writes
Fail-open locks — split-brain risk in multi-worker deployment
Redis stream IDs for event sequencing — breaks Last-Event-ID int contract
Full hash DELETE on stale cleanup — clobbers parallel manual runs
No stale lock detection — accept false 409s until TTL
Per-process INCR counters — out-of-order writes across workers
outcome: 86 new tests, 8 Codex findings resolved, zero regressions. 4 Redis keys in schema.

task: Structured Logging Layer 2 — Correlation & Context Propagation
approach: 8-phase plan: (1) get_context_value + scoped_bind helpers, (2) X-Request-ID + middleware hardening, (3) LangSmith trace linkage, (4) SSE context binding, (5) Auth failure logging, (6) Per-step/per-agent binding, (7) run_id in runners, (8) async propagation tests
rationale: Completes structured logging story — every log line traceable from HTTP request through pipeline step through LangSmith trace. X-Request-ID separate from X-Correlation-ID for proper distributed tracing. scoped_bind context manager prevents context leaks across sequential pipeline steps.
alternatives_rejected: Explicit ContextVar objects alongside structlog — dual source of truth with no benefit
Pure ASGI middleware for request-id — too big a refactor for marginal gain
Bind trace_id at each callsite instead of in tracing.py — not DRY, 14+ changes
outcome: 48 new tests, zero regressions. 3 backlog items resolved (PB-83, PB-84, PB-85). All 6 pipelines enriched with step/agent context.

task: Async-first pipeline conversion approach
approach: Convert all I/O-bound steps to async using AsyncOpenAI, httpx.AsyncClient, asyncio.to_thread for ChromaDB
rationale: Pipeline was ~57 min worst case due to sequential HTTP calls. Async with semaphore-based concurrency provides ~5x speedup with minimal architecture changes.
alternatives_rejected: aiohttp + aiolimiter (adds inconsistent second HTTP client)
anyio wrapping for ChromaDB (over-engineering, asyncio.to_thread works fine)
async-stdlib.bounded_gather (over-engineering for BFS crawl)
outcome: All 7 tasks complete. 58 tests passing. Expected ~57min → ~11min pipeline time.

task: Cloudflare bypass strategy for s1 crawler
approach: 3-tier fallback chain in _crawl_one: httpx (fast) → Playwright headless Chromium (CF bypass) → Wayback Machine (last resort). Site-level flag skips httpx after first CF detection.
rationale: Cloudflare-protected sites (carta.com) return 403 to all httpx requests. Playwright is already in requirements.txt. Wayback Machine provides historical content as last resort.
alternatives_rejected: cloudscraper library (fragile, constantly breaks as CF updates)
Proxy rotation (cost, complexity, still blocked by JS challenge)
Skip CF-protected sites (unacceptable — Carta is a client)
outcome: Implementation complete. Awaiting live test on carta.com.

task: Content Generation Engine architecture
approach: 4-stage async pipeline: Strategic Planner (Sonnet) → Orchestrator-Workers (Sonnet/Haiku/Perplexity) → Evaluator-Optimizer (4 dimensions, 2 revision cycles) → LangGraph HITL. Raw AsyncAnthropic SDK, semaphore concurrency, Langfuse tracing.
rationale: Follows two proven Anthropic patterns: Orchestrator-Workers for parallel content production, Evaluator-Optimizer for automated QA. Reuses existing async/semaphore patterns from gap analysis. LangGraph HITL matches research pipeline pattern.
alternatives_rejected: LangChain wrappers (inconsistent with gap analysis, hides control)
CrewAI multi-agent (over-engineering, deterministic chain sufficient)
Single monolithic LLM call (no quality control, no parallelism)
outcome: Full implementation complete. 57/57 tests passing. 30+ files created across core/content_engine/, tests/content_engine/, scripts/.

task: Codex review findings incorporated into content engine plan
approach: Incorporated 8 critical findings from Codex o3 review: return_exceptions=True in gather, safe_parse() for LLM JSON, retry for Anthropic errors, context window guard, directory creation, early exit for max_revision_cycles=0, StructuralTargets model, word_count_range tuple.

task: FastAPI integration architecture — asyncio.create_task, JSON TaskStore, SSE events, MemorySaver HITL
approach: Same-repo api/ package. asyncio.create_task (not Celery), JSON-file-backed TaskStore, SSE for progress, MemorySaver checkpointer for HITL interrupt/resume. pydantic_settings.BaseSettings for env-var config.
rationale: Lightweight, no infra deps. JSON files are simple and debuggable. asyncio.create_task matches existing async-first patterns. MemorySaver enables LangGraph checkpoint/resume for HITL approvals.
alternatives_rejected: Celery + Redis (over-engineering for current scale)
WebSocket for progress (SSE is simpler, auto-reconnect via Last-Event-ID)
SQLite TaskStore (unnecessary complexity, JSON files are sufficient)
outcome: 6 phases complete. 126 tests passing. All 3 pipelines wrapped with REST endpoints, SSE events, and HITL approval flow.
tech_debt_warnings: model_dump(mode='json') in TaskStore persistence — works fine in Pydantic v2 but verify with future Pydantic upgrades

task: S4 main content extraction — dual-soup architecture
approach: Two separate HTML processing paths: _extract_main_content() uses trafilatura for clean text extraction (paragraphs), _extract_structural_html() uses semantic-tag-only scoping for element counting (preserves ol/dl/table/details).
rationale: Trafilatura gives best text quality but flattens structural HTML elements (ol→p, dl→p, details→p). Semantic tags preserve structure for counting. Dual approach gets best of both.
alternatives_rejected: Trafilatura-only (loses structural element counts — ordered_list_count=0, definition_list_count=0)
BeautifulSoup-only (doesn't handle nav/footer/sidebar contamination well enough)
Custom content extraction (reinventing what trafilatura already does well)
outcome: S4 now produces ~45 structural signals. Word counts are realistic (800-3000 vs previous 7-43555). All 351 tests passing.

task: GapContentBrief naming and 3-tier output architecture
approach: Named GapContentBrief (not ContentBrief) to avoid collision with content_generation.ContentBrief. gap_analysis_complete.json is additive — existing 3-file contract (gap_report.json, generation_spec.json, analysis.json) unchanged.
rationale: Content engine's run_content_engine.py (lines 93-106) loads 3 separate JSON files. Breaking this contract would require coordinated changes. New file is a superset for future consumption.
alternatives_rejected: Replace gap_report.json with combined file (breaks content engine loading)
Name it ContentBrief (collision with downstream model)
outcome: Both models coexist. 3-file contract preserved. gap_analysis_complete.json available for new consumers.

task: Phase 1 auth and data model architecture — JSON-file backed, pre-Supabase
approach: JSON-file backed AuthStore for companies+users (artifacts/_auth/), PBKDF2 password hashing, HMAC-signed JWT-like tokens, grace-mode middleware. UserProfile uses first_name/last_name (not single name field). Company model has additional_domains for subdomain tracking.
rationale: Simple, no external dependencies, easy to migrate to Supabase later. Grace-mode middleware allows incremental auth rollout without blocking unauthenticated requests. Separate first_name/last_name is standard for user profiles.
alternatives_rejected: bcrypt for password hashing (requires extra C dependency, PBKDF2 is sufficient for v0)
PyJWT for tokens (over-engineering for v0 — HMAC-signed base64 is simple and replaceable)
Single name field (harder to personalize UI, less professional)
outcome: AuthStore working with full CRUD, registration with company dedup, 423 tests passing.

task: Registration flow — company deduplication by normalized domain
approach: normalize_domain() strips protocol/www/path/port, handles multi-part TLDs (.co.uk, .com.au), returns (root_domain, subdomain_or_none). Registration matches by root domain — first user becomes superuser, subsequent users join as member. Subdomains preserved in company.additional_domains.
rationale: Domain normalization prevents duplicate companies created from variations (app.ramp.com vs www.ramp.com vs ramp.com). Multi-part TLD handling prevents incorrect root extraction (example.co.uk should not become co.uk). Subdomain preservation captures seed URLs for future crawling.
alternatives_rejected: Email domain verification (deferred — adds friction, not needed for v0)
Manual company creation only (bad UX, doesn't scale)
tldextract library (adds dependency for something we can handle with a simple frozenset)
outcome: Registration endpoint working with 25 TDD tests covering edge cases.

task: Phase 2 gap data endpoints — URL routing and backward compatibility
approach: Separate prefix /api/v1/companies/{slug}/gap-analysis/ (not /api/v1/gap-analysis/) to avoid conflicts with existing /api/v1/gap-analysis/{run_id}/status endpoint. Fallback chain: gap_analysis_complete.json → analysis.json + gap_report.json for backward compatibility with Ramp's old format (11 structural signal fields, no content_brief).
rationale: Existing gap analysis endpoints are run-management (start, status, cancel). Data endpoints are resource-oriented (read pre-computed artifacts by company slug). Separate URL namespace keeps concerns clean. Backward compat ensures Ramp's existing data works without re-running the pipeline.
alternatives_rejected: Nest under existing /api/v1/gap-analysis/ prefix (URL collision with run_id paths, confusing semantics)
Require re-run for old format (bad UX, wastes compute for data that's already valid)
Single monolithic endpoint returning all data (too large for paginated queries, inflexible)
outcome: 6 endpoints working with both old and new artifact formats. 61 tests covering both formats.

task: Gap data service — caching and computation strategy
approach: Module-level mtime-based cache (max 10 entries, FIFO eviction). All computed metrics (Pearson correlations, Jaccard similarity, signal averages, cluster fingerprints) computed on-the-fly from raw artifacts. Platform engine names mapped to lowercase frontend keys (openai→chatgpt, etc.).
rationale: Artifacts are static between pipeline runs, so mtime-based invalidation is simple and correct. On-the-fly computation avoids stale pre-computed caches. Module-level cache handles repeated requests within a session. FIFO is acceptable for small cache size.
alternatives_rejected: Pre-compute metrics at pipeline completion (couples pipeline to API concerns, duplicates work if frontend schema changes)
Redis cache (over-engineering for single-server deployment)
No caching (enriched_citations.json can be ~20MB, re-parsing on every request is wasteful)
outcome: Working with acceptable performance. Known thread-safety issue (C6) deferred to .claude/sprints/v1/.

approach: Fix 4 critical issues blocking frontend integration now: C1 (missing login/me endpoints), C2 (AuthMiddleware not registered), C3 (no email/password validation), C4 (auth data not gitignored). Defer remaining 20 issues to .claude/sprints/v1/review-findings-deferred.md.

Only fix C1 (leaves security gaps — auth data would be committed without C4)

task: Product-level pipeline execution — effective_slug design and prompt injection strategy
approach: Double-underscore separator `{company_slug}__{product_slug}` for artifact dirs and lock keys. `effective_slug` stored on `PipelineTask`. Central `RunScope` dataclass + `_resolve_scope()` helper in runner.py. Research artifacts inherit from company slug (ordered fallback chain: effective_slug → company_slug → None). Product prompts injected via `{product_context_block}` slot (empty string for company-level runs). Guard condition: inject only when `product_slug AND product_name` both non-null. `_SLUG_PATTERN` in all 3 service files extended to `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*(__[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?$` to accept effective slugs.
rationale: Double underscore is unambiguous since individual slugs use `[a-z0-9-]` only. Storing effective_slug on PipelineTask eliminates re-derivation in all 4 teardown paths (3 runners + cancel endpoint). Central _resolve_scope() makes product lookup DRY. Inheritance fallback means product runs can leverage company research without re-running it. Empty-string default for product_context_block means zero prompt drift for company-level runs.
alternatives_rejected: Single underscore separator (ambiguous if slug ever contains underscores)
Separate artifact trees per product without inheritance (duplicates research artifacts, wastes storage)
Separate prompt files per product level (unnecessary — injection is DRY and safe)
Compute effective_slug in each of 11 data endpoint handlers (drift risk)
outcome: All 5 phases complete. 882 tests passing (114 new). Company-level and product-level locks are independent (ramp and ramp__corporate-card can run concurrently). Same product locks properly conflict.
codex_review: Codex gpt-5.3-codex pre-implementation review incorporated 6 CRITICAL + 7 WARNING findings. Key: lock teardown mismatch fixed via task.effective_slug, cross-tenant auth via product.company_id == user.company_id, artifact inheritance explicit ordered chain, prompt guard condition.

task: Switch embedding model from text-embedding-3-large (3072) to text-embedding-3-small (1536)
approach: Changed settings.embedding_model default to text-embedding-3-small. Updated all test fixtures (mock settings, dimension sizes). Updated all documentation references (CLAUDE.md, README.md, COMPREHENSIVE_SYSTEM_DOCUMENTATION.md).
rationale: text-embedding-3-small is sufficient for semantic proximity analysis. Halves embedding storage and computation cost (1536 vs 3072 dims). No code changes needed beyond settings default — all code reads settings.embedding_model dynamically.
alternatives_rejected: Keep text-embedding-3-large (unnecessarily expensive for gap analysis cosine similarity)
Use a different provider (Cohere, Voyage) — would require client changes
outcome: Embedding model changed. 351 tests passing. All docs updated. Existing artifacts with 3072-dim embeddings will need re-embedding on next pipeline run.

task: Route protection & authorization — default-deny middleware, RBAC, tenant isolation, invite flow
approach: Pure ASGI middleware (not BaseHTTPMiddleware) for default-deny auth with explicit public path whitelist. FastAPI dependencies for RBAC (require_auth, require_role) and tenant isolation (require_tenant). Registration hardened to create isolated companies only — joining existing companies requires invite codes. Stream tokens (5min, stream_only flag) for SSE EventSource clients. JWT_SECRET_KEY enforcement in non-dev environments.
rationale: Codex gpt-5.3-codex review found 6 CRITICAL issues (C1–C6) in the grace-mode auth system: cross-tenant registration, client-controlled tenant scoping, IDOR task endpoints, query-param token leakage, fail-open grace mode, deleted user authorization. All incorporated into this 9-phase implementation. Pure ASGI middleware avoids BaseHTTPMiddleware's known issues with SSE streaming (W1). Dependency-based auth allows per-endpoint role granularity.
alternatives_rejected: Keep BaseHTTPMiddleware (risky for SSE streaming — Codex W1)
Token-based tenant scoping only (no server-side validation — Codex C2)
Full bearer tokens as query params for SSE (leaks in logs/referrer — Codex C4)
Domain-based auto-join registration (cross-tenant account takeover — Codex C1)
Email-based invite system (over-engineering for v0 — simple codes sufficient)
Middleware-level role checks (mixes auth + authz concerns, less flexible)
outcome: 944 tests passing. Default-deny on all routes. RBAC enforced. Tenant isolation verified. Invite flow working. Stream tokens for SSE. 42 dedicated auth enforcement tests.
codex_review: Codex gpt-5.3-codex with xhigh reasoning effort. 20 findings: 6 CRITICAL, 10 WARNING, 4 INFO. All CRITICALs and relevant WARNINGs incorporated. Plan at .claude/plans/bright-skipping-cupcake.md.

task: Existing-company pipeline guard — prevent duplicate runs for users joining analyzed companies
approach: force_rerun: bool = False on GapAnalysisStartRequest + ResearchStartRequest. Guard fires BEFORE task_store.create_task(). Gap analysis: dual-sentinel (gap_analysis_complete.json OR analysis.json). Research: stage-aware _research_stages_exist() checks only requested stages, excludes .draft.md personas. Both return HTTP 200 with already_exists=True, stable run_id (last completed task or f'existing-{effective_slug}').
rationale: Dual-sentinel mirrors gap_data_service.py:112 consistency. Stage-aware research guard prevents blocking legitimate partial-stage re-runs (e.g., stages=['persona'] when only company context exists). Guard before create_task avoids triggering 409 slug conflict. f'existing-{effective_slug}' fallback is non-empty and stable so frontend doesn't crash on status polling.
alternatives_rejected: Single-sentinel (gap_analysis_complete.json only) — breaks for companies with only s6 output
Coarse research guard (any artifact exists) — blocks partial-stage runs (Codex C1)
Include .draft.md in persona check — false positives (Codex C2)
list_tasks()[0] for last run — unsorted, cross-scope contamination (Codex C3)
Empty run_id='' fallback — breaks frontend status polling (Codex C4)
outcome: 12 new tests. 900 tests passing total. Feature 2 (Content-Gap Integration) deferred to future sprint — design preserved in .claude/plans/cozy-twirling-mochi.md.
codex_reviews: 2 rounds of Codex gpt-5.3-codex high-reasoning review. Round 1: 5C+7W (scope included Feature 2). Round 2: 4C+6W (Feature 1 only). All criticals incorporated.

task: Settings Pages API + Knowledge Doc Upload — architecture and shared module extraction
approach: File-backed settings (artifacts/_auth/settings/{slug}.json) + knowledge docs with _metadata.json sidecar. Shared modules in core/shared_tools/ (text_extraction.py for canonical .md/.txt/.pdf/.docx extraction, knowledge_doc_metadata.py for single process-wide metadata_lock + atomic I/O). Pipeline defaults merge: request > company defaults > global settings. Knowledge docs auto-included in s1 embedding with discovery_source='knowledge_doc'. Runner resolves knowledge_doc_dir with product→company fallback.
rationale: File-backed storage continues the existing pattern (auth store, task store). Shared modules prevent code duplication and ensure thread safety between concurrent upload + pipeline execution. core/shared_tools/ is the correct location since core/ cannot import from api/. Auto-include all knowledge docs is simpler UX than per-doc selection.
alternatives_rejected: Redis-backed settings (over-engineering for single-server)
Per-doc include/exclude toggle (unnecessary complexity — delete docs you don't want)
Separate lock per metadata file (same process, same GIL — single lock is simpler and sufficient)
pdfminer instead of pdfplumber (pdfplumber has cleaner API for text extraction)
Phase 1D API keys in this sprint (deferred — pre-YC we run with our own keys)
outcome: 6 phases + 6 review fixes complete. 1029 tests (77 new). 11 new API endpoints. Shared modules eliminate code duplication and prevent race conditions.

task: SQLAlchemy + Alembic migration Phase 1 — ORM choice, schema design, repository pattern
approach: Pure SQLAlchemy 2.0 Declarative (NOT SQLModel). Native PgUUID(as_uuid=True) for PKs. Lazy engine initialization (no import-time DB connections). Hand-written Alembic migrations (not autogenerated). HNSW indexes split into separate migration 0002. Generic repo base with flush-only contract (DI session generator owns commit/rollback). 12 Postgres enum types. 31 ORM tables matching 30-table schema (url_structural_signals is 1:1 extension of url_enrichment_cache). Savepoint-based test isolation with after_transaction_end restart logic.
rationale: SQLAlchemy 2.0 wins 6-0 scorecard vs SQLModel across pgvector Vector(1536), 12+ Postgres enums, JSONB with server_default, ARRAY(Text), self-referential FK, and Alembic autogenerate. We already maintain 3 model layers (core Pydantic, API schemas, ORM) with explicit repo conversion — SQLModel's dual class provides zero benefit. Hand-written first migration avoids known autogenerate footguns with pgvector/enums/partial indexes. Flush-only repos enable savepoint test isolation AND multi-repo atomic transactions. Codex gpt-5.3-codex review with extra-high reasoning identified 10 CRITICAL + 8 WARNING findings, all incorporated.
alternatives_rejected: SQLModel (dual Pydantic+ORM class unnecessary in our architecture, escape hatches for pgvector/enums)
String(36) PKs (16 bytes vs 36 bytes per PK/FK, slower indexing — native UUID is correct for Postgres)
Autogenerated first migration (known issues with pgvector extensions, enum creation, partial indexes)
Combined HNSW+schema migration (HNSW index creation locks tables in production)
Separate database_url_sync env var (drift risk — computed property from database_url eliminates it)
Repos owning commit() (breaks savepoint test isolation, prevents multi-repo atomicity)

task: Auth Migration Phase 2 — Three-layer decomposition of AuthStore into async DB-backed AuthService
approach: Layer 1: Pure utility extraction to core/auth/utils/ (passwords, tokens, domain). Layer 2: AuthServiceProtocol (runtime_checkable Protocol) + JsonAuthService (wraps AuthStore via asyncio.to_thread) + DbAuthService (uses DB repos). Layer 3: DI switch via get_auth_service() — returns DbAuthService if DATABASE_URL set, else JsonAuthService. Middleware decoupled from AuthStore — uses verify_token utility + app.state.secret_key directly. All routers migrated from sync def→async def, all auth_store params→auth_service. Runner has both _resolve_scope (sync, CLI) and _resolve_scope_async (async, routers).
rationale: Dual-mode adapter strategy enables zero test breakage — existing 1080 tests pass via JsonAuthService wrapping AuthStore. Utility extraction enables middleware to operate without any service dependency. Protocol-based interface enables seamless swap from JSON to DB backend without touching any router code. Async-first design prepares for production DB usage.
alternatives_rejected: Direct AuthStore replacement (would break all 1080 tests at once — high risk)
Keep sync endpoints with sync DB calls (blocks on DB I/O, defeats async architecture)
Single AuthService class with conditional logic (violates SRP, harder to test)
Full middleware rewrite (unnecessary — only needed to decouple from AuthStore)
outcome: 18 new files, 32 modified files, 96 new tests. 1080 passed + 88 skipped = 1168 total. All existing tests pass unchanged via dependency override. Plan at .claude/plans/vectorized-honking-flamingo.md.

task: Service Layer Migration Phase 3 — Three separate service protocols with dual Json/Db implementations
approach: Following the proven auth migration pattern (AuthServiceProtocol → JsonAuthService / DbAuthService), each data domain gets its own Protocol: GapDataServiceProtocol, BrandDataServiceProtocol, ContentDataServiceProtocol. Each has a JsonXxxService (wraps existing api/services/ functions via asyncio.to_thread) and a DbXxxService (uses SQL repos). Routers converted from sync def → async def with service injection via Depends(). DI functions default to JsonService, switch to DbService when DATABASE_URL + db_session_factory available. Filesystem operations (embedding projections, research artifacts, stage content) remain filesystem-backed even in DB services via asyncio.to_thread delegation.
rationale: Separate protocols keep interfaces narrow and testable — each service has different dependencies (gap needs signal/platform repos, brand needs pipeline repo, content needs content repo). The Json→Db switch is transparent to routers. SQL aggregation replaces Python computation for heavy operations (AVG on 45 structural signals, corr() for Pearson correlations). Platform agreement Jaccard kept in Python per Codex W4 recommendation. Backfill script enables testing with real data without Phase 4 write hooks.
alternatives_rejected: Single monolithic DataServiceProtocol (violates SRP, bloated interface, different dependency sets per domain)
Direct DB queries in routers (couples routers to DB, untestable)
Pure SQL for Jaccard computation (fragile, hard to test — Codex W4)
Skip Json wrappers, go DB-only (breaks all existing tests, no fallback)
outcome: 16 new files, 14 modified. 3 service protocols + 6 implementations (3 Json + 3 Db). 2 new repos (signal, platform) + 3 enhanced repos. Backfill script for JSON→DB migration. 46 new tests (9 protocol conformance passed + 37 DB tests skipped). 1088 passed + 125 skipped = 1213 total. Plan at .claude/plans/glowing-soaring-turtle.md.
codex_review: Codex gpt-5.3-codex with high reasoning reviewed the plan before implementation. 2 CRITICAL + 5 WARNING findings incorporated: C1 GapClassification enum drift fix, C4 slug resolution UUID-scoped, W1 composite indexes, W2 NULL safety in SQL, W3 empty runs return 200, W4 Jaccard in Python, W5 parity tests.

task: TaskStore DB Migration — Protocol + DbTaskStore + lifespan DI switch
approach: TaskStoreProtocol (runtime_checkable Protocol) mirroring existing TaskStore API. DbTaskStore uses write-through pattern: state transitions write to DB via asyncio.create_task(), in-memory dict for fast sync reads. Startup recovery loads non-terminal tasks, marks orphans as failed_restart. ApiTaskModel ORM with plain String status (not PG enum, because TaskStatus includes pending_approval/failed_restart). Lifespan _init_task_store() tries DbTaskStore when DATABASE_URL set, falls back to JSON TaskStore on failure. Session factory per-operation (not request-scoped).
rationale: Single-instance durability: task history persists across restarts, queryable task data. Protocol-based interface enables transparent swap. Write-through ensures DB durability for state transitions while keeping sync reads fast. Plain String status avoids PG enum limitations. Fallback to JSON ensures zero-downtime for existing deployments without DB.
alternatives_rejected: Write-behind (loses durability guarantees — Codex CX-13)
PG advisory locks for slug locks (over-engineering — in-memory locks sufficient for single instance)
PG enum for status column (missing pending_approval/failed_restart values — Codex CX-3)
Request-scoped sessions for DbTaskStore (long-lived singleton, not request lifecycle — Codex CX-4)
JSON→DB migration script (out of scope — DbTaskStore starts fresh, JSON preserved as-is — Codex CX-7)
outcome: 5 new files (protocol, DbTaskStore, ORM model, repository, migration). 7 files migrated to protocol type hints. 49 new tests. 1127 passed + 135 skipped = 1262 total. Horizontal scaling (multi-worker SSE, distributed cancellation) deferred — requires Redis pub/sub or PG LISTEN/NOTIFY.
codex_review: Codex gpt-5.3-codex with high reasoning. 14 findings: 7 INCORPORATED (CX-1 scope, CX-3 enum, CX-4 sessions, CX-6 cancellation, CX-9 /me tests, CX-10 get_company_by_id, CX-13 write-through), 4 REJECTED (CX-2 sync/async, CX-5 advisory locks, CX-7 migration script, CX-8 PB-28/29 reorder), 3 DEFERRED (CX-11 API spec, CX-12 test estimates, CX-14 false positives). Plan at .claude/plans/sleepy-moseying-charm.md.

task: Daily Tracker Integration — Orchestrator (Mediator), FastAPI router, DI wiring
approach: Mediator pattern orchestrator coordinates prompt library, platform runner, and mention detector — no direct module-to-module communication. Stateless orchestrator returns DailyRunResult (no DB dependency). API router provides 16 endpoints (8 prompt CRUD, 3 run management, 5 analytics) with auth/tenant isolation. DI layer in api/dependencies.py provides 3 factory functions (get_prompt_library_service, get_analytics_service, get_daily_tracker_orchestrator) with app.state override pattern for test injection. _DbResponseDataProvider adapter bridges DB repos to AnalyticsService's ResponseDataProvider protocol.
rationale: Mediator pattern keeps modules decoupled — adding new modules (e.g., notification service) requires changes only in the orchestrator. Stateless orchestrator enables pure-mock testing (no DB setup needed). DI factory functions follow existing app.state override pattern (consistent with other routers). _DbResponseDataProvider adapter keeps analytics engine decoupled from storage — it can work with any data provider implementing the protocol. All 503 responses on missing DB ensure clear failure mode vs silent degradation.
alternatives_rejected: Direct module-to-module calls (tight coupling, harder to test, harder to extend)
Orchestrator owns DB persistence (mixes orchestration with storage, harder to test)
Inline analytics computation in router (violates SRP, duplicates calculation logic)
Single monolithic DI function for all services (harder to override individually in tests)
outcome: 66 new tests (20 orchestrator + 46 API). All passing. 16 endpoints operational with auth enforcement. Mediator pattern verified — orchestrator only depends on 3 protocol interfaces.

task: Content Engine Pipeline v1.3 — two-phase context loading, LiteLLM, dual feedback loops, E-E-A-T
approach: 6-stage pipeline running alongside v1.0: (1) scorecard extraction (~11K tokens) for planner triage, (2) full context per-topic for Brief Builder, (3) workers accept ContentBlueprint (subclass of ContentBrief), (4) 5-dimension evaluator with dual feedback (section-level vs major-change), (5) 3 HITL checkpoints via LangGraph interrupt(). LiteLLM wraps all LLM calls (workers, judges, agents). v1.0 preserved as-is. Workers modified in-place (swap SDK call → llm_call), shared between both pipelines. _ensure_litellm_model() auto-prefixes model strings for backward compat.
rationale: Full gap analysis output (80-120K tokens) created context explosion for the v1.0 planner. Two-phase loading reduces planner context to ~11K tokens. ContentBlueprint extends ContentBrief so all existing workers accept it transparently (zero type hint changes). LiteLLM provides model abstraction for benchmarking + easy provider switches. Dual feedback loops prevent expensive re-briefs from automated evaluator false positives — major direction change only from HITL-3 human rejection or semantic score < 0.5. E-E-A-T adds content quality signal missing from v1.0's 4-dimension evaluation.
alternatives_rejected: Separate v1.3 worker copies (90% code duplication, maintenance nightmare)
Replace v1.0 pipeline entirely (breaks existing content runs, no fallback)
LangChain for LLM abstraction (inconsistent with gap analysis, hides control)
Runtime prompt pulls from LangSmith Hub (adds availability dependency — prompts stay in Python files)
Major direction change from automated evaluator (too expensive, false positive risk)
outcome: Phases A-D1-D2 complete. 14 new files created, 9 files modified. 211 content+research tests passing. v1.0 pipeline fully preserved. Workers shared between both pipelines via LiteLLM.
key_design_points: ContentBlueprint extends ContentBrief — transparent to all workers
_ensure_litellm_model() auto-prefixes: claude-* → anthropic/, sonar* → perplexity/, gpt-* → openai/, gemini-* → google/
classify_feedback() returns pass/section_level/major_change — section_level is default loop
use_eeat=False and use_targeted_revision=False defaults preserve v1.0 behavior
Three composed LangGraph sub-graphs with interrupt() at each HITL gate

task: Content Engine v1.3 D3 — Defer full lightweight gap analysis for manual mode to PB-45
approach: Keep the current inline approach: pipeline_v13.py lines 363-404 construct a WorkerQueryContext directly from the user's manual_prompt without running gap analysis stages s3-s6. The inline context provides topic, intent, and a minimal exemplar structure sufficient for Brief Builder to produce a valid ContentBlueprint.
rationale: Full s3-s6 reuse adds 2-5 min latency for manual mode (search 4 platforms + enrich + embed + analyze). It also requires s1 output (SemanticUnit list) as prerequisite, which doesn't exist for manual-mode users who haven't run gap analysis. The current inline WorkerQueryContext is sufficient for v0 — Brief Builder can produce useful blueprints from just a topic string + intent.
alternatives_rejected: Run full s3-s6 for manual mode (2-5 min latency, requires s1 prerequisite that may not exist)

task: Content Engine v1.3 Pipeline Refactor — Phases 4-10 (25-point gap closure)
approach: 10-phase implementation closing 25 gaps between v1.3 current state and target flow. Key changes: (1) Forward 5 brief builder fields (gap_reasoning, tone_voice_description, target_persona, buyer_stage, intent_stage) through outliner→drafter. task: Question-heading classification without trailing ?
approach: Classify wh-word headings (how/what/why/when/where/who/which) as questions even without trailing ?, with >= 4 words guard. Auxiliary verbs (is/can/does/etc.) still require ?.
rationale: AI engines DO extract 'How to...' headings as Q&A. Guard prevents false positives on fragment headings like 'How' or 'What Now'.
alternatives_rejected: Require ? for all headings (under-reports AEO)
No word-count guard (false positives on fragments)
outcome: 10 new tests passing. AEO scores more accurate for well-structured content.

task: Quick-answer word range expansion 15-150
approach: Expand from hardcoded 30-70 to configurable 15-150 via AuditConfig fields (aeo_quick_answer_min_words, aeo_quick_answer_max_words). Search bounded by heading elements.
rationale: FAQ answers often 15-30 words, detailed answers 70-150. Current range missed both. Heading boundary prevents matching unrelated paragraphs.
alternatives_rejected: Keep 30-70 (misses valid content)
Unbounded search (matches wrong sections)
outcome: 10 new tests passing. Config fields allow reverting to any range.

task: Missing date finding for article pages only
approach: Generate low-severity missing_date_metadata finding only when page_type == 'article'. Non-article pages unaffected.
rationale: AI models deprioritize undated articles. Homepage/product/pricing pages don't need date metadata.
alternatives_rejected: Flag all page types (over-penalizes non-articles per Codex F-3)
No finding at all (misses real issue)
outcome: 5 new tests passing. Article freshness accuracy improved.

task: Crawl-delay parse+report only, no enforcement
approach: Parse Crawl-delay from robots.txt, cap at 300s, report as findings (info >10s, medium >30s). Rate-limiting enforcement deferred.
rationale: Enforcement requires shared domain-level rate limiter (asyncio.Lock + timestamp) — separate feature. Parse+report provides immediate value.
alternatives_rejected: Full enforcement (too complex for P3 fix)
No findings, just data field (less actionable)
outcome: 12 new tests passing. Clients see if robots.txt throttles AI bots.

task: Split canonical URL from request URL for dedup
approach: New canonical_url() for dedup (sorts params, strips www, removes default ports, normalizes percent-encoding). normalize_url() unchanged for HTTP requests.
rationale: Sorting query params in request URL breaks signed URLs and param-order-sensitive endpoints (Codex F-4).
alternatives_rejected: Sort params in normalize_url (breaks signed URLs)
No param sorting (poor dedup)

alternatives_rejected: langchain.agents.create_agent (different return type, breaks test assertions)
Raw LangGraph StateGraph builder (over-engineering for a simple tool-calling agent)
outcome: Synthesis agent builds and runs correctly. Deprecation warning is cosmetic.

approach: web_search_20250305 server-side tool with _MAX_PAUSE_TURNS=5 iteration guard. api_key passed explicitly from settings.

task: Model string format for init_chat_model
approach: Colon separator (anthropic:claude-opus-4-6). _build_model helper handles colon, slash, and bare formats.

Bare model name (requires provider auto-detection)
outcome: Settings use colon format. _build_model handles all 3 formats for flexibility.

task: KB orchestrator pattern — pipeline-with-inline-HITL vs monolithic LangGraph
approach: Pipeline function owns execution flow. LangGraph mini-graphs only for HITL pause/resume (interrupt/Command). asyncio.gather for parallel agents.
rationale: DAG phases involve asyncio.gather for parallel agents within phases, which is trivial in async Python but complex in LangGraph topology. Each HITL checkpoint needs different approval payloads. Mode handling (full/refresh/single) is conditional logic that belongs in the pipeline. Same pattern as pipeline_v13.py.
alternatives_rejected: Monolithic LangGraph StateGraph (complex topology for parallel phases, hard to handle 3 modes)
Pure async pipeline with no LangGraph (lose interrupt/resume for HITL)
outcome: pipeline.py owns 4-phase DAG + 3 modes. graph.py provides 2 HITL sub-graphs (doc review shared for CP1/CP2, synthesis for CP3). run_kb_hitl_checkpoint helper mirrors graph_v13 pattern.

task: Revision note injection — re-run agents with feedback vs re-run from scratch
approach: Inject revision_note as '## Reviewer Feedback' section appended to user prompt. All 6 prompt builders + agents got backward-compatible Optional[str] param.
rationale: Re-running from scratch wastes API calls and time. Reviewer feedback is specific and targeted — appending it to the prompt lets the agent address it in context of its full research. Backward-compatible (default None).
alternatives_rejected: Re-run agent from scratch (wasteful, loses context)
Store revision notes in state and pass to synthesis only (loses per-doc specificity)
outcome: All 6 prompt builders append '## Reviewer Feedback' when revision_note is provided. Pipeline re-runs only the docs that received revise feedback. 9 tests cover injection + passthrough.

task: HITL helper — self-contained in KB module vs extracted shared utility
approach: Keep run_kb_hitl_checkpoint in core/research/knowledge_base/graph.py. Do not extract to shared utility yet.
rationale: KB and content engine HITL have different state schemas, interrupt payloads, and approval semantics. Extracting a shared utility prematurely would create coupling. Can extract later when patterns stabilize.
alternatives_rejected: Extract to core/shared_tools/hitl.py (premature abstraction — KB and content engine differ enough)
outcome: KB HITL helper is self-contained. Mirrors graph_v13 pattern but is independent. Tested with 22 graph tests.

task: Self-citation handling in avg_citation_similarity
approach: Keep company self-citations IN the avg_citation_similarity calculation. Add separate fields (company_cited, company_cited_platforms) as explicit signals for the content engine.
rationale: avg_citation_similarity measures 'how well do cited pages align with the query.' The company being cited is a valid data point. Excluding it would break existing metric interpretation. Separate fields give the content engine explicit signal to adjust strategy (optimize vs create new).
alternatives_rejected: Exclude self-citations from avg_citation_similarity (breaks metric semantics, loses valid data point)
outcome: company_cited + company_cited_platforms fields on QueryGap. Strategic Planner and Brief Builder prompts updated to handle cited vs uncited strategies.

task: Company structural analysis: per-page model vs per-chunk signals
approach: Create separate CompanyPageAnalysis model (per-page) rather than adding StructuralSignals to SemanticUnit (per-chunk).
rationale: SemanticUnit is per-chunk (10-20 per page). Duplicating 45-field StructuralSignals across all chunks wastes storage and is semantically wrong — structural signals describe a page, not a chunk. CompanyPageAnalysis is URL-keyed and stored once per page.
alternatives_rejected: Add structural_signals to SemanticUnit (wastes storage, semantically incorrect — signals are page-level not chunk-level)
outcome: CompanyPageAnalysis model in gap_analysis.py. s1 computes signals per page via s4's compute_structural_signals(). Saved to company_page_analysis.json. s6 attaches to QueryGap via URL lookup.

task: Self-citation flagging timing — before or after s4 dedup
approach: Flag company citations on PlatformResult BEFORE s4 enrichment, and build company_citation_map BEFORE s4 dedup.
rationale: s4 dedup collapses multi-engine citations into a single EnrichedCitation. If flagging happens after dedup, we lose which engines cited the company. _flag_company_citations runs in pipeline.py after s3, _build_company_citation_map also runs before s4.
alternatives_rejected: Flag after s4 dedup (loses multi-engine information)
outcome: _flag_company_citations() and _build_company_citation_map() in pipeline.py, called between s3 and s4. is_company_citation carried through s4 dedup into EnrichedCitation.

task: Replace ChromaDB with pgvector as primary vector store
approach: 8-phase migration: VectorStoreClient with drop-in API, 2 Alembic migrations, EmbeddingRepository extensions, consumer migration, full ChromaDB removal, data migration script.
rationale: ChromaDB is local SQLite-backed, single-process — not production-ready. pgvector infrastructure already existed (3 tables + HNSW indexes + EmbeddingRepository). Migration makes pgvector PRIMARY and ONLY store, requires DATABASE_URL.
alternatives_rejected: In-memory fallback without DATABASE_URL (undermines production readiness)
Keep ChromaDB alongside pgvector (dual-write complexity, maintenance burden)
outcome: ChromaDB fully removed. VectorStoreClient (469 lines) is single write path. persist_s1 is no-op (VectorStoreClient writes during S1). persist_s5 handles query embeddings only. Codex-reviewed: 11 findings, all addressed.

task: Consolidate persist_s1/s5 with VectorStoreClient
approach: persist_s1 → logging-only no-op (VectorStoreClient writes during S1 execution). persist_s5 → query embeddings only (needs run_id FK not available in VectorStoreClient). Citation paragraph embeddings handled by VectorStoreClient during S5.
rationale: Single write path eliminates double-writes. Query embeddings require run_id FK (pipeline_runs table) which is only available in pipeline context, not in VectorStoreClient.
alternatives_rejected: Full no-op for persist_s5 (loses query embedding persistence)
Pass run_id through VectorStoreClient (coupling pipeline concerns into vector store)
outcome: Clean separation: VectorStoreClient handles embeddings, persist_s5 handles query embeddings with run_id FK.

task: Deterministic enrichment IDs for S4 FK integrity
approach: Replace uuid4() with uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, url_hash) in persist_s4 for enrichment IDs.
rationale: uuid4() generates new IDs on every rerun, breaking FK references from paragraph_embeddings.url_enrichment_id. uuid5 is deterministic — same URL always produces same enrichment ID.
alternatives_rejected: Query existing enrichment IDs before insert (extra DB round-trip)
Remove FK constraint (loses referential integrity)
outcome: Deterministic IDs prevent FK mismatch on reruns. Pre-existing bug fixed during migration.

task: Structured logging library choice — structlog vs python-json-logger
approach: structlog with stdlib ProcessorFormatter bridge. Single configure_logging() call at app startup. JSON renderer for prod, ConsoleRenderer for dev. Context propagation via structlog.contextvars.
rationale: structlog's contextvars integration natively propagates bound fields (correlation_id, company_slug) into every log record. stdlib bridge means zero changes to 115 existing logging.getLogger() call sites. Dev/prod renderer switching built-in. Codebase already uses contextvars for LangSmith tracing.
alternatives_rejected: python-json-logger (requires building context propagation with custom logging.Filter by hand, always outputs JSON)
Pure stdlib dictConfig + JSON formatter + ContextVar filter (more code, less battle-tested, reinventing structlog)
outcome: 22 new tests, 2 new files, 13 modified files. All 1063 API tests passing with zero regressions. Codex-reviewed (6 findings incorporated).
